modifier_claims.support_quote: Several foci showed papillary projections lined by multilayered epithelium with atypical cells, few mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis but no dermal invasion

She had had a lesion at that site since childhood, which had remained asymptomatic and pea sized for most of that time. However, over the 10 years prior to presentation it had gradually increased in size and became itchy. There was also occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding from the lesion.

Examination revealed a 1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine. Adjoining skin showed a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification.

- Histopathological examination:    - Revealed a circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining    - Tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
